disposition_reason: Eight vegetables and three fruits bought from vendors at four market sites in Bareilly, India were analysed for Al, As, Cd, Pb and Hg by AAS; Table 3 prints mean ± SD per food on a dry-weight basis.

study.design: Market survey of commonly consumed fruits and vegetables
study.origin: not stated (area irrigated with water from the industrially polluted Ramganga River, per the study-area description)
study.market: Local vendors and shops at four market sites, Bareilly city, Uttar Pradesh, India

period.as_reported: Summer; foods chosen after a dietary survey in May-June 2018 (collection dates not otherwise stated)

study.method: Oven drying at 80 C, HNO3/H2SO4/HClO4 digestion on a hot plate, graphite furnace AAS (Thermo iCE 3000)
study.qa: no CRM, recovery or blank data reported

unresolved: No detection limits, reference materials or recoveries are reported, and mercury is stated to be measured by graphite furnace AAS without a cold-vapor or hydride step, so analytical quality cannot be checked.
Number of samples per food and per market site not stated; market sites are pooled.
Comparison with dry-weight results against fresh-weight limits is the authors' own; not reconciled.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Permissible limits used by the authors (sources cited as refs 14 and 7)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Al 1, As 0.05, Hg 0.01 mg/kg; Cd 0.05-0.2, Pb 0.1-0.2 mg/kg by food (Table 2)
